item.title: Men are from Mars, Women are from Venus
item.description:
Quotes

Setting limits and receiving are very scary for a woman. She is commonly afraid of needing too much and then being rejected, judged, or abandoned. Rejection, judgment, and abandonment are most painful because deep inside her unconscious she holds the incorrect belief that she is unworthy of receiving more. This belief was formed and reinforced in childhood every time she had to suppress her feelings, needs, or wishes.

A young boy who is fortunate enough to see his father succeed in fulfilling his mother enters relationships as an adult with a rare confidence that he can succeed in fulfilling his partner. He is not terrified of commitment because he knows he can deliver. He also knows that when he doesn’t deliver he is still adequate and still deserves love and appreciation for doing his best

item.title: How to Find Love
item.description:
Author: The School of Life

Our belief in instinct has been no friend of our chances of happiness. We can’t go back to the Marriage of Reason, but we may need to look for a future beyond the Relationship of Instinct.

If we intend to get better at relationships, we must attempt to examine the calls of Romantic love rationally. This isn’t a question of abandoning instinct, but of improving upon it.

item.title: The Charisma Myth
item.description:
• Charisma feels real.
  • When we first meet someone, we instinctively assess whether that person is potential friend or foe.
  • When you meet a charismatic person, you get the impression that they have a lot of power and they like you a lot.

Charisma in conversation

  • Do these:
    • Lower intonation at the end of sentences.
    • Reduce how quickly and how often you nod.
    • Pause for two full seconds before you speak.
  • If you’re not fully present in a conversation, there’s a good chance that your eyes will glaze over or facial reactions will be split-second delayed. Human mind can read facial expressions in as little as 17 ms, so the other person will notice even the tiniest delays in your reactions.
  • Aim to bring yourself back to present by focusing on your toes or breath for a second, and then focusing on the other person.
  • Being charismatic doesn’t depend on how much time you have but on the presence in a conversation.
  • Figuring out who might want to help us and has power to do so has always been critical to our survival. That’s why our reaction to power and warmth is wired so deep.

Body Language

  • We can’t micromanage charismatic body language.
  • If we can direct our subconscious directly, then our nonverbal signals will be solved.
  • Charismatic behaviors originate in the mind since people can see change in briefest micro-expression.
  • Knowing your internal world starts with one key insight upon which all charisma is built: your mind can’t tell fact from fiction.

Components of charisma

  • Presence : When you exhibit presence, those around you feel listened to, respected, and valued.
  • Power
  • Warmth

Interactions

  • To the outside world, your face will show the same reaction to discomfort from the sun as it would to feelings of anger or disapproval.
  • When interacting, assume that other person will feel that whatever you do relates to him/her.
  • Signs of fatigue can easily show up in people’s body language as lack of enthusiasm.
  • If something from outside is irritating you such as construction sounds, take a moment to explain that you are in discomfort. Giving voice to something will generally allow both parties to move on from it.

Tolerance

  • Our inability to tolerate uncertainty carries multiple costs. It can cause us to make immature decisions. It can handicap us in negotiations, leading us to reveal more than we should as we scramble to fill the silence, unable to bear the uncertainty of not knowing what the other person is thinking. Anxiety is a serious drawback to charisma.

Disbelief

  • Faking belief to be assured.

Our brains are wired first to understand, then to believe, and last to disbelieve. Since disbelief requires additional cognitive effort, we get the physiological effects first. And, though this belief may last only a brief moment, it’s enough to produce an emotional and physical reassurance, which can change our thought patterns as well as help alleviate the uncomfortable feelings.
